ai_assessment.method: Full direct English-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 4669 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported about forty major and about two hundred and ten minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.24; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: “Amethyst” rendered as ruby; corrected to the amethyst sense.
Same amethyst error, repeated; corrected.
“Six children” rendered as seven; corrected to the English count.
A question assigned to the wrong speaker (Fred and his mother); corrected.
Rosamond’s innuendo assigned to her mother; corrected.
“Few things worth the pains” was inverted to “fewer things worth the effort”; restored.
Larcher’s skimping of attendance was rendered as making it a luxury; restored.
“Chị tôi” used for Celia, the younger sister; corrected.
Solomon’s seniority reversed and the English “Brother” left in Vietnamese; corrected.
Keble’s “The Christian Year” rendered as the year “Năm Thiên Chúa”; corrected.
Sir James’s “put that color on it” garbled; corrected.
Business “kept for” Dorothea, reversed from “kept from”; corrected.
A double negation reversed on Lydgate’s marriage; corrected.
Pronouns reversed in Rosamond’s complaint; corrected.
Dorothea called Celia’s “em vợ”; corrected to the elder-sister form.
“Nam tước” used for baronet in the precedence joke; corrected.
The Tipton cousins’ “dubiously mixed” blood was attributed to the Freshitt children; the irony restored.
Will Ladislaw given as Casaubon’s nephew where the source says cousin; corrected.
“Proteges” rendered as “người”; corrected to the English sense.
“On the fifth day after the meeting” read as Thursday; corrected.

summary: All 4669 units of the complete novel as printed by Project Gutenberg #145, translated directly from the English. The first blind reviews of the five parts scored between 8.24 and 8.7 with about forty major findings across them, mostly referents, speakers, address forms, rank and sense reversals. Each part was revised in fix rounds, and separate-context blind reviews re-checked each revision; the named majors listed here are the ones verified against the English. The final reviews score the parts 8.90 (Book I and the Prelude), 8.85 (Books II–III), 8.68 (Books IV–V), 8.75 (Books VI–VII, with one disputed major at unit 3952, where the witness reads ‘Balstrode’ and the translation follows it) and 8.73 (Book VIII and the Finale). The weakest part, 8.68, sets the score. Minor findings are recorded in the review files and do not block release.

title_review.rationale: The title is the work’s own, ‘Middlemarch’, the name of the town; the Vietnamese edition keeps the English title.
